hints: Look closely at the white (unshaded) group in each diagram. One group, CH3 in this example, is different in other amino acids, so can it be part of the common structure?

Recall the four groups attached to the central carbon in every amino acid: hydrogen, amino group, carboxyl group, plus the variable R group. Which shaded set includes all the first three and leaves out only the R group?
walkthrough:
**Recall what every amino acid shares**

Every amino acid has the same backbone. A central carbon atom joined to a hydrogen atom (H), an amino group (NH2) and a carboxyl group (COOH).

The fourth group is the R group, here CH3, and this is the only part that varies.

**Check the diagrams for the variable part**

The CH3 group is the R group for this amino acid (alanine). It is not common to all amino acids, so the correct shaded set must leave CH3 white and shade everything else.

**Pick the matching diagram**

Only diagram B shades H, C, NH2 and COOH together, and leaves just CH3 unshaded. That is exactly the part common to all amino acids.

options.A: Shades H, C and COOH but leaves NH2 white. The amino group is part of every amino acid, so this set is incomplete.
options.B: Shades H, central C, NH2 and COOH, leaving only the variable R group (CH3) white. This is the backbone common to all amino acids.
options.C: Shades the variable R group CH3 and leaves H and COOH white. It includes a variable part and misses common parts.
options.D: Shades CH3 along with the common groups but leaves H white. It wrongly includes the variable R group and misses hydrogen.
